data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"A decentralized network of small services is more resilient to correlated failure only if its 'Infrastructure Overlap' (the intersection of dependency trees) is lower than the 'Coordination Complexity' of a large service's redundancy management.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The decentralized services all rely on a single critical shared dependency (e.g., a specific DNS provider or BGP route).","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The large service implements 'True Heterogeneity' (multi-stack, multi-cloud) under a decoupled control plane.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Resilience is a function of diversity (heterogeneity) versus control. In a decentralized network, the lack of a central control plane removes a single point of failure but introduces 'Common Mode Failures' via shared libraries or cloud providers. A large service's redundancy is often 'homogeneous redundancy' (more of the same), which fails identically under the same stress. The decentralized network wins when the variety of its implementations (different OS, languages, providers) exceeds the failure-inducing overlap of its shared dependencies.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
